Subject: Renewal options + quick true-up idea

Hi Alicia —

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our discussion I pulled together three close-form renewal options (attached) that balance unit economics with short-term predictability while leaving room for the growth pattern you outlined. High level:

- Option A: 12-month renewal, 10% baseline discount, automated monthly true-up (no penalties).
- Option B: 12-month renewal with a 6-week price hold on Q1 consumption and 150K one-time credit, then standard tiered rates.
- Option C: 24-month renewal with a deeper discount and committed burst pool (preferred for heavy seasonal spikes).

I included a proposed staged uplift for the first 90 days (prefix caching + burst pool) to cover the projected ramp you mentioned. If procurement wants a one-page amendment, I can draft it and run it through RevOps.

Attached: Finera_Renewal_Options_v3.pdf (PDF, 4 pages).

Marcus —

Appreciate the clear set of options and the fast turnaround. A couple of constraints from our side:

1) Finance has asked that we *hold pricing for the first quarter* of the renewed term (Q3 start) to avoid volatility during our product launch. We can commit to a twelve-month term but need a temporary price hold window.
2) We expect a burst in usage at launch; procurement wants to avoid surprise overage invoices. Is there a way to include a short-term burst pool (25% increase) that is credit-backed for the first 90 days?
3) Can you share our Q2 usage so we can model true-up projections?

I’ve attached our internal Q2 extracts. Procurement loops in here for their input.

If you can draft language for a price-hold clause + conditional burst pool, procurement can route faster.

Thanks Alicia — that context is helpful. Looping in Ben (Sales Manager) and Neha (RevOps / Finance) so we can confirm what’s doable on our side.

Quick proposal from Redwood to address the three asks:

- Price hold: we can offer a *temporary price hold for the first full quarter* of the renewed term (matches your ask) but ask that the customer commit to a 12-month renewal and an automated monthly true-up to reconcile delta consumption.
- Burst pool: we can provision a *credit-backed burst pool* equal to 20% of the committed baseline for the first 90 days. Any usage above that will either draw from committed capacity or be billed at the overage rate; we will not invoice overages during the 90-day window if the uplift is within the agreed burst bucket.
- One-time credit: we can extend a one-time onboarding credit of 150K to offset initial variability (applies at signing).

If that sounds in line with procurement’s tolerance, I’ll put the language into an amendment and open a DocuSign for signature. Ben / Neha — can you confirm internal approval thresholds for the 20% burst bucket and 150K credit? If needed we can trade deeper discount for a larger committed uplift.

Alicia, Marcus —

Quick internal decision: we can approve a revised offer with the following firm terms (we prefer to keep it binding to avoid churn risk):

1) Price hold: 12% price hold on current effective rates for the first quarter of the renewed term.
2) Commit: 12-month renewal commitment. In exchange for the hold we require a 15% uplift in baseline committed capacity (measured as average monthly tokens across the last 3 months baseline).
3) Burst pool: 20% credit-backed burst for the first 90 days (as Marcus suggested). Any sustained usage above 20% that carries beyond 90 days will be converted into the committed baseline for the remainder of the term and billed pro rata.
4) One-time credit: $150,000 applied against the first invoice at signing.
5) True-up: automated monthly true-up (no retroactive penalties), with data reconciliation window of 30 days.

Next steps: Marcus will prepare an amendment with excerpted clause language and we’ll route via DocuSign. Alicia — if those terms are acceptable, please confirm and I’ll set up the signature packet.
